NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MAC No. 954 of 2015  Krishna Kumar S/o Narmada Prasad Swarnakar, Aged About 53  Years, R/o Village Urga, District Korba, Chhattisgarh  ---- Appellant  Versus
1. Suresh Singh Thakur S/o Rajput Thakur, Aged About 19 Years  R/o Bhaisma (Faikapahari), Chowki Urga, Tahsil And District  Korba, Chhattisgarh  2.

The New India Insurance Company Limited, Branch Office, T.P.
 Nagar, Korba, District Korba, Chhattisgarh

---- Respondents For Appellant : Mr. T. K. Tiwari, Advocate For Respondent No.1 : None For Respondent No.2 : Mr. Chitram Sahu, Advocate, on behalf of  Mr. Sourabh Sharma, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Judgment On Board 13.06.2024 1.

Present is an owner's appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act challenging the award dated 19.06.2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Korba (CG) in Claim Case No.07/2010 whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.2,10,392/- with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the injured claimant and against the appellant.
2.

In this case, the accident took place on 12/03/2009 at about 6 p.m. when appellant Krishna Kumar driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.CG 04 CD 3859 rashly and negligently Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19197 dashed the motorcycle on which claimant Suresh Singh Thakur Krishna Kumar vs Suresh Singh Thakur on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51419914/
1 was traveling as a pillion rider.

entities.text: Suresh Singh Thakur Krishna Kumar vs Suresh Singh Thakur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On account of the accident, the right femur and Tibia Fibula bone of Claimant Suresh Singh got fractured and during treatment a rod was inserted in his leg after surgery.
Claimant Suresh Singh preferred a claim application before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.14,75,000/-.
Learned Claims Tribunal, on a close scrutiny of the evidence available on record, assessed total compensation of Rs.4,20,784/-.

However, considering 50%
contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the motorcycle on which the claimant was travelling as a pillion rider, the Tribunal has awarded 50% of total compensation amount i.e.
Rs.2,10,392 /- in favour of the claimant with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of application till its realization.

While passing the impugned award, the Tribunal has reached to the conclusion that from the evidence available on record it has been clearly established that the offending motorcycle was being driven in violation of the insurance policy condition and therefore the Insurance Company was exonerated of its liability and the liability of payment of compensation saddled upon the driver/owner of the offending motorcycle i.e. the appellant.
It is this fastening of liability of payment of compensation upon the driver/owner against which the present appeal has been filed by the owner.

3. The first ground of challenge to the impugned award by learned counsel for appellant is that at the time of accident the appellant did have a driving licence and therefore, there was no breach of policy condition and the Tribunal has erred in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.

The second ground of challenge to the impugned award is that since there was a valid policy covering the offending motorcycle at the time of accident, the Tribunal ought to have applied the principle of "pay and recover".
Hence, prays for issuance of an order of "pay and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19197 recover".

In support of its contention learned counsel for appellant placed his reliance upon a decision of this Court in the case of Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Shabana Khan and others passed on 21.09.2022 in MAC No.322 of 2015.
4.

entities.text: Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Shabana Khan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company i.e. respondent no.2 opposes the prayer of the counsel for appellant and submits that at the time of accident the driver of the offending motorcycle did not have a valid effective driving licence and therefore, the finding of the Claims Tribunal holding the driver/owner liable for payment of 50% of the compensation is just and proper and requires no interference in the same.
It has also been argued that the prayer for pay and recover principle cannot be made by the registered owner.
5. There is no representation on behalf of the claimant respondent no.1.

6. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

So far as the first ground of the appellant regarding valid driving licence is concerned, learned Tribunal, in Para- 13 & 14 of its award, after considering the evidence brought on record and discussing this issue in detail has held that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid effective driving licence, therefore, there is a clear breach of policy condition.

Hence, the Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability which in the opinion of this is a proper finding and therefore, the first ground of the appellant is not acceptable.
Krishna Kumar vs Suresh Singh Thakur on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51419914/
2 8.

entities.text: Krishna Kumar vs Suresh Singh Thakur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the second ground of "pay and recover" sought for by the counsel for appellant, this Court is of the opinion that since it is an appeal by the owner, the said principle cannot be made applicable in an appeal preferred by the owner.
The said principle Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19197 can be applied only in the event of the appeal being that of the Insurance Company or for that matter the claimant.

In the judgment relied upon by the appellant, nowhere it has been observed/held that the owner can pray for an order of "pay and recover", therefore, the said judgment is distinguishable on its facts itself and would not give any benefit to the appellant.
9.
In view of the same, this Court does not find any strong case made out by the appellant calling for an interference with the impugned award.
The appeal being devoid of merit deserves to be and is accordingly dismissed.

Sd/-
(Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) Judge Khatai Krishna Kumar vs Suresh Singh Thakur on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51419914/
